title: EIP-8321: Hash-Chain RANDAO
description: Replace the BLS-signature RANDAO reveal with a post-quantum hash-chain commit-reveal scheme
author: Kevaundray Wedderburn (@kevaundray), Benedikt Wagner (@benedikt-wagner), Tom Wambsgans (@TomWambsgans), Justin Drake (@JustinDrake), Thomas Coratger (@tcoratger)
laymanDescription: Ethereum's randomness depends on each proposer's signature being the only one it could possibly have produced. A quantum computer could recover a validator's key and predict every future contribution, and the planned post-quantum signature lacks that uniqueness. This proposal replaces the signature with a chain of hashes.
benefits: Rests on hash properties believed to hold against quantum attack, not on BLS uniqueness
Costs one 32-byte commitment per validator and one hash check per proposal
Unregistered validators keep using the old path, so no cutover deadline is needed
tradeoffs: A commitment can never be updated, so a lost or mistyped chain forces exit and re-entry
Introduces a chain secret needing the same custody as a signing key
Block signatures and the registration itself stay BLS, so the transition is incomplete
